Subject: RE: Unit economics deep-dive / Pricing qualification — quick math

Jordan — adding a quick unit-economics sketch so you have concrete numbers ahead of our call. I kept it conservative and used your ramp profile from the attachment. See the attached redwood_pricing_model_v2.xlsx for the working tab; below are highlights and assumptions.

Assumptions (pilot -> ramp):
- Pilot: 300M tokens/mo
- Ramp: 1.2B tokens/mo (midpoint target)
- Your target revenue per month (pilot): $50k–$70k

Redwood cost and margin illustration (simplified):
- Example inference cost (hosted, optimized open model) = $250–$400 per 1M tokens (depends on model and quantization).
- Dedicated reserved capacity (committed) can reduce inference cost to ~$150–$250 per 1M tokens at scale.

If FintechX target = $700 / 1M tokens (customer-facing charge), then:
- Hosted scenario (cost $300 / 1M): gross margin ≈ (700 - 300) / 700 = ~57%
- Dedicated scenario (cost $200 / 1M): gross margin ≈ (700 - 200) / 700 = ~71%

$/feature example (high level):
- Example feature: credit-decision assistant charged as part of product.
- Assumed usage per active user: 2k tokens/month
- If you price the feature at $0.50 / active user (per month), tokens per 1k users = 2M tokens -> feature revenue = $500 / 1k users -> cost @ $200/1M = $400 -> gross margin = 20% (low)
- To hit a healthier margin (50%+), either increase price to ~$1.00 / user/month or reduce inference cost per 1M to <$150 via dedicated/quantization/efficient model.

CAC payback example (illustrative):
- If the feature drives $10k incremental ARR and CAC per customer is $60k (example), payback is long. But if the feature increases ARPU by $3/user/month and you acquire 20k users via targeted channels, payback compresses to <9 months. We’ll tailor this math to your exact acquisition and pricing assumptions in the workbook.

Next steps for the call:
- I’ll walkthrough the sensitivity table: inference cost per 1M (x-axis) vs gross margin and required price per feature (y-axis).
- Bring your product finance or growth lead if possible — they can confirm ARPU and CAC assumptions.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_model_v2.xlsx (pricing scenarios and sensitivity), I’ve also included a quick one-page summary in the workbook.

Best — Ben
